title: Preflight: GPU upgrade preflight & fallback playbook (sandbox rehearsal)
content:
Summary:
This document captures the sandbox rehearsal we ran for GPU driver/CUDA/NCCL upgrades across k8s node pools and the associated terraform module adjustments and fallback paths. The goal is to validate an upgrade corridor that lets us move from driver series 520.x -> 535.x -> 545.x (and CUDA 11.8 -> 12.1 -> 12.2) without prolonged downtime for Dedicated/Private clusters. Notes are intentionally operational and include failures seen, short-term mitigations, and recommended terraform interface changes for safer rollouts.

Context & scope:
- Environment: private VPC cluster (k8s) in AWS-like sandbox (custom AMI), 3 nodepools (gpu-small, gpu-medium, gpu-large).
- Workload types tested: inference microbenchmarks (gpt-small batching), long-lived transformer training replica (stress memory/cuda), multi-node NCCL allreduce smoke (2x nodes).
- Versions tried in rehearsal: k8s 1.25/1.26/1.27, NVIDIA drivers 520.61 / 535.86 / 545.45, CUDA 11.8 / 12.1 / 12.2, NCCL 2.14 / 2.17 / 2.18.

High-level findings (observed behaviours):
- Kubelet + driver upgrade ordering matters: restarting kubelet before driver unload leads to stale device files and crashloop pods.
- Driver 545 introduced a delayed init on some Ampere nodes (observed 45–90s extra boot time) due to a missing firmware blob in our custom AMI; caused transient scheduling pressure.
- NCCL 2.18 interop with CUDA 12.2 passed our distributed allreduce tests, but under high PCIe busy signals we saw increased timeouts (tunable via NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING).
- Container runtime edge case: containerd 1.7 + cgroup v2 + nvidia-container-runtime had a race where devices were not published to the container if driver install happened concurrently with CRI restart.
- Observed kernel oops (rare) when switching between 520.x -> 545.x without full node reboot; risk reduced if we fully power-cycle or re-create nodes.

Failure modes and impact matrix:
- driver-install-failure (nvidia-installer exit != 0): pod eviction + node unschedulable — impact: high on heavy-load services; mitigation: fail fast and rollback node to previous AMI in terraform.
- device-node-missing (/dev/nvidia* absent): workload crash — impact: medium; mitigation: preflight probe that checks /dev and nvidia-smi before marking node ready.
- kubelet-race-on-driver-reload: kubelet restarts drop IPC handles — impact: medium-high; mitigation: ensure daemonset that replaces driver pauses kubelet restart until drivers present.
- firmware-missing: increased boot latency and possible cgroup scheduling backlog — impact: low-medium; mitigation: include firmware files in AMI and add preflight checksum.

Concrete terraform/infra changes proposed (short bullets):
1) node_pool.driver_upgrade_strategy = "recreate" | "in-place-with-reboot" selector. Default: recreate for critical pools.
2) add preflight_hook (local-exec) step that runs an image to validate device nodes and runs nvidia-smi -L; if fails, abort apply.
3) create terraform-managed rolling_recreate_count + max_unavailable parameter per pool.
4) add AMI manifest versioning and a tag gpu-firmware-checksum so TF can assert AMI contains required blobs.
5) provision a temporary warm standby nodepool (drain target) to keep capacity during upgrades for enterprise customers.

Suggested terraform snippet (conceptual; put in module interface):
# module gpu_node_pool args
# driver_upgrade_strategy = "recreate" | "in-place-with-reboot"
# preflight_image = "gcr.io/redwood-sandbox/gpu-preflight:202508"

Operational runbook (rehearsal-tested):
1) Create upgrade branch and change nodepool AMI+driver refs.
2) Spin up 1st canary node in a disabled autoscaling pool (Terraform apply).
3) Run preflight container: docker run --rm --privileged gcr.io/redwood-sandbox/gpu-preflight:202508 
   - checks: nvidia-smi -L, /dev/nvidia* present, nvml test vector, simple CUDA kernel run (vector add).
4) If preflight passes, attach canary to kube cluster and run smoke inference load for 10–15m. Monitor p999 latency and GPU utilization.
5) Promote to rollout: recreate nodes in small batches (configurable). For each node: cordon, drain, destroy node resource (force destroy) then create replacement with target AMI.
6) Observe cluster-level health (control plane metrics, pod restarts).
7) If any canary fails, immediately revert nodepool module to previous AMI and invalidate new instances; run terraform apply.

Smoke tests & validation commands (copy-paste):
- nvidia-smi -q | head -n 40
- docker run --rm --gpus all nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s/cuda-sample:vectorAdd && echo OK
- kubectl -n perf run loadgen --image=ghcr.io/redwood/loadgen:gpu --restart=Never -- /bin/sh -c "python3 load.py --model=gpt-small --iters=200"
- NCCL multi-node: run our nccl-tests container with N=2 nodes and check allreduce time 99th pct < baseline*2.

Essential logs to capture during failure:
- dmesg (look for nvidia/PCIe errors), journalctl -u kubelet, /var/log/nvidia-installer.log, /var/log/cloud-init-output.log, containerd/cri logs, kubelet /var/log/kubelet.log.
- Collect nvml logs via nvidia-smi --debug and SCCS if available.

Observability & SLO thresholds for upgrade window:
- p999 latency for inference routes must not exceed baseline by > 2x for more than 5 minutes.
- error rate increase < 0.5% absolute.
- node replacement time (cordon->ready) < 12m median.

Rollback & fallback patterns tested:
A) Fast rollback: mark new instances unhealthy in ASG & destroy; terraform apply to re-add old nodepool AMI. Works when driver install fails early.
B) Soft-fallback: keep old nodepool autoscaled for 48h and route low-priority traffic to new pool. If instability continues, shift production traffic back and decommission new nodes.
C) Emergency: full account snapshot + rebuild (longer path) — tested once, takes ~2.5h for our sandbox scale.

Lessons learned from rehearsal (operational):
- Always include firmware blobs in AMI where possible; driver-only installs are brittle across kernel versions.
- Prefer recreate (replace) semantics for major driver bumps instead of in-place upgrades unless you control power cycles.
- Small canaries with the full load profile (including batch sizes and KV cache warmups) catch subtle NCCL/cuda regressions earlier.
- Add a short (60s) quiesce period after kernel module updates before kubelet restarts to let udev settle.

Open questions / next steps:
- Decide default driver_upgrade_strategy per customer tier (dev/staging/prod).
- Automate preflight results reporting into Console (rollup + warning banner for affected tenants).
- Should we add driver verification step into Dedicated onboarding? (Pros: fewer production-time surprises. Cons: longer provisioning.)
- Validate same process on heterogeneous clusters (mixed Ampere + Hopper nodes) — we saw one-time variance during our multi-arch tests.

Owners & timeline:
- Maya Chen: drive terraform module PR and preflight image (2 weeks).
- Carlos Rivera: update AMI build pipeline to include firmware + checksum (1 week).
- Priya Nair: integrate preflight results with Console banners (3 weeks).

Appendix: quick checklist to run locally (sandbox)
- checkout infra/gpu-nodepool branch
- terraform apply -var 'nodepool=canary' -auto-approve
- kubectl apply -f tests/nccl-allreduce.yaml
- run nvidia preflight container and review output
- collect logs if any test fails and attach to JIRA INF-2134

If you run this plan, paste raw logs to the linked JIRA and ping #eng-private-deployments.

---
Revision note: initial rehearsal 2025-08-14, added mitigation steps 2025-08-18 after second run, finalized checklist 2025-08-21.
